interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, today we have an opportunity to take stock of the results of the intense work carried out over the last number of years. The revised Victims' Rights Directive, as provisionally agreed on 10 December 2025, is now ready to be adopted.

I would like to start by expressing my sincere appreciation for the work of this House and to each of you honourable Members in achieving this outcome, and of course, in particular to the core rapporteurs, Lucia Yar and Javier Zarzalejos, all of the shadow rapporteurs who contributed, and all of the Members of the House who made important contributions. Thank you for your work. Thank you for your steadfast commitment to supporting victims of crime in the European Union. And thank you for your willingness to compromise so that we could get a tangible outcome by way of an agreed legislative file in the end.

The negotiations between the co-legislators were fruitful and constructive, and were conducted in a true spirit of interinstitutional cooperation. This demonstrates that we share a common goal to enhance the support, protection and access to justice for victims of crime all across the European Union. The new rules will significantly reduce the procedural and emotional burdens for victims, laying the foundation of a truly victim‑centred approach that we have long endeavoured to achieve.

Victims of crime endure trauma and harm, and they must never face secondary or repeat victimisation when in contact with the criminal justice system. And we know that this has happened in all too many cases that we are familiar with. The list of improvements is extensive, and every right under the current Victims' Rights Directive has been further strengthened in this proposal. Member States will now be required to establish helplines for victims, offering confidential information, guidance and emotional support. Reporting crimes will become easier with secure online options and greater opportunities for victims to participate in criminal proceedings. Victims will receive support in dedicated court spaces, with additional psychological support available to those who need it. The new directive will also streamline access to compensation from offenders and will improve coordination and cooperation among professionals interacting with victims of crime.

This Commission has made a strong commitment to protecting children from harm, violence and other online threats, and to upholding children's rights. The revised directive reinforces this commitment, I am pleased to say. Child victims of crime will benefit from tailored, integrated support and protection based on important multi-agency cooperation and individual assessments of their needs, because each case is different. This is a milestone towards achieving genuine child‑friendly justice, and I know we will continue to work together to achieve this goal. Other vulnerable victims, such as victims with disabilities, will also benefit from comprehensive access to support services and from procedural accommodations, which can be important for them too.

In summary, these new rules and elevated standards will ensure that millions of victims of crime in the EU will receive better protection, support and access to justice. The Commission stands ready to support Member States in the transposition of this directive, once this House and the Council have both completed the formal adoption.

However, we must recognise – and I know the honourable Members in this House do – that legislation alone is not enough. It's real‑world application that determines its success. To further strengthen the legal and policy framework and support victims' rights, the Commission will adopt, by the end of this year, a new EU strategy on victims' rights. The strategy will outline clear actions at both EU and national level to support the enforcement of these new rules on the ground, so that the lived experience of victims of crime in the European Union is better in the future than – I think we all know – it has been in the past in too many cases.
So thank you for your collective work. I look forward to the vote tomorrow, but also to the contributions of all of you in the House here this evening.

interventions.speaker_label: Rosa Estaràs Ferragut, en nombre del Grupo PPE.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, está claro que con la Directiva 2012/29/UE, por la que se establecen normas mínimas sobre los derechos, el apoyo y la protección de las víctimas de delitos, y durante su aplicación se detectaron deficiencias. Básicamente porque las víctimas desconocían sus derechos, no denunciaban suficientemente y, además, no recibían el apoyo adecuado a sus necesidades concretas.

Por eso, esta nueva Directiva corrige todas estas dificultades y establece un enfoque basado en la persona. Esto es fundamental, porque en esta Directiva se tiene en cuenta el género, si una persona tiene discapacidad, si es un menor y las circunstancias de las víctimas. Por lo tanto, se aborda el tema de forma personalizada. Eso es muy importante, especialmente para los colectivos vulnerables, como menores y personas con discapacidad, porque esta Directiva lo que hace es adaptar, hacer accesible todo el procedimiento de victimización, y, por lo tanto, es muy importante para este colectivo.

El acceso digital a la justicia, también con adaptaciones accesibles, es importante como complemento a los canales tradicionales. Se refuerza también el número europeo de ayuda a las víctimas con el número europeo para menores desaparecidos, víctimas de violencia de género o el teléfono de infancia. Se facilita, sin ninguna duda, la posibilidad de denunciar, eliminando muchos obstáculos que hasta ahora había para las denuncias, reforzando la privacidad y también la protección de datos. Son muy importantes los servicios de apoyo especializados, gratuitos y accesibles; son clave, así como reforzar el acceso a la asistencia jurídica eficaz y, por supuesto, la información durante todo el proceso a todas las víctimas.

Hay un tema importante: en el caso de las víctimas de violencia sexual, tendrán garantizado el acceso a los servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva y el acceso al aborto de acuerdo con el principio de subsidiariedad.

En definitiva, los derechos de las víctimas deben ser claros, accesibles y exigibles, y, por supuesto, debe haber medidas de protección contra el terrorismo y los delitos graves. La glorificación de estos delitos supone una vulneración de la dignidad de las víctimas.
Enhorabuena a los ponentes, Javier Zarzalejos y Lucia Yar, por este importante trabajo.

Esto es fundamental, porque en esta Directiva se tiene en cuenta el género, si una persona tiene discapacidad, si es un menor y las circunstancias de las víctimas. Por lo tanto, se aborda el tema de forma personalizada. Eso es muy importante, especialmente para los colectivos vulnerables, como menores y personas con discapacidad, porque esta Directiva lo que hace es adaptar, hacer accesible todo el procedimiento de victimización, y, por lo tanto, es muy importante para este colectivo.

El acceso digital a la justicia, también con adaptaciones accesibles, es importante como complemento a los canales tradicionales. Se refuerza también el número europeo de ayuda a las víctimas con el número europeo para menores desaparecidos, víctimas de violencia de género o el teléfono de infancia. Se facilita, sin ninguna duda, la posibilidad de denunciar, eliminando muchos obstáculos que hasta ahora había para las denuncias, reforzando la privacidad y también la protección de datos. Son muy importantes los servicios de apoyo especializados, gratuitos y accesibles; son clave, así como reforzar el acceso a la asistencia jurídica eficaz y, por supuesto, la información durante todo el proceso a todas las víctimas.

Hay un tema importante: en el caso de las víctimas de violencia sexual, tendrán garantizado el acceso a los servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva y el acceso al aborto de acuerdo con el principio de subsidiariedad.

En definitiva, los derechos de las víctimas deben ser claros, accesibles y exigibles, y, por supuesto, debe haber medidas de protección contra el terrorismo y los delitos graves. La glorificación de estos delitos supone una vulneración de la dignidad de las víctimas.

Enhorabuena a los ponentes, Javier Zarzalejos y Lucia Yar, por este importante trabajo.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Alessandro Zan, a nome del gruppo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, cosa succede quando subisci un reato d'odio e lo Stato non ti riconosce? Succede che subisci due traumi: il reato e l'indifferenza delle istituzioni.

Domani, in quest'Aula, votiamo la direttiva "Vittime", una legge europea storica – e lo dico con orgoglio, da relatore per il gruppo dei Socialisti e Democratici – per i risultati raggiunti per tutte le vittime, come il rafforzamento della privacy e il supporto medico‑psicologico post‑traumatico, compreso l'accesso all'aborto sicuro per le vittime di violenza sessuale. Per la prima volta, infatti, si menziona l'aborto in una legge dell'Unione europea.
Inoltre, affermiamo un principio fondamentale: chi viene colpito per il proprio orientamento sessuale, la propria identità di genere, il genere o la disabilità merita una protezione speciale.

L'odio lascia ferite profonde e la legge deve riconoscerlo. È uno dei principi cardine di quello che è stato il ddl Zan, che nel 2021 veniva affossato tra gli applausi vergognosi dell'estrema destra al Senato italiano e oggi, con l'approvazione di questa direttiva, può tornare dall'Europa a tutti gli Stati membri, compresa l'Italia.
Perché la giustizia non si misura solo per come punisce, ma anche per come protegge.

interventions.speaker_label: Margarita de la Pisa Carrión, en nombre del Grupo PfE.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidente, señor comisario, señorías, con la modificación de esta Directiva teníamos una oportunidad histórica para velar por el respeto de las víctimas y de sus familias.

Todavía hoy en España se celebran homenajes —ongi etorri— a terroristas asesinos de ETA, por lo que la tipificación del delito de glorificación del terrorismo hubiera sido crucial y no se ha conseguido por falta de valentía política, siguiendo la estela de Sánchez de complacer y blanquear el terrorismo.
Eso sí, se ha puesto la alfombra roja para que se siga avanzando en la imposición de una agenda ideológica que se impone a los Estados, sin importar las incoherencias con sus legislaciones.

Ha sido triste ver el empeño de la mayoría de los grupos de esta Cámara —incluido el Partido Popular— por introducir por primera vez en una legislación europea la mención explícita al aborto como un servicio al que tienen derecho las mujeres víctimas de múltiples tipos de delitos, no solamente violencia sexual. Realmente, este era el objetivo político. Lo acaban de celebrar ustedes, señorías, a pesar de que, para haberlo conseguido, se haya tenido que renunciar a otro tipo de protecciones a las víctimas importantes.

Las víctimas merecían una Directiva centrada en su dignidad, en sus derechos y en la defensa de su memoria, pero, una vez más, las prioridades de esta Cámara han sido otras: utilizar el dolor de las víctimas como vehículo para seguir imponiendo una agenda ideológica que nadie ha votado.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the ECR Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, I would like to ask you this: imagine a young girl, sitting somewhere, defenceless, full of life and joy. But someone decides at that very moment that you are their prey. They impose themselves on you because they can. And because they know that they can get away with it. Too many people got away with it already.
In this situation, only the law can make a difference. This is why, as parents and as lawmakers, we must make the difference, beyond political divides, to ensure that our laws do not have flaws.

I was born, myself, in a culture where your destiny was determined on the basis of sex. I'm grateful to live on a continent where our destiny is based on equality and fundamental rights. But yet, injustice prevails.

We are here today to say that protecting victims is more important than what divides us. And I would like to dedicate this speech to my daughter Axelle, who is now upstairs, looking at us and having a lot of hope. Thank you to all my colleagues.

interventions.speaker_label: Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle, namens de Renew-Fractie.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, commissaris, geweld tegen vrouwen neemt toe en het komt voor het overgrote deel uit eigen kring. Een op de vijf vrouwen in Europa heeft te maken met een vorm van gendergeweld. Recent onderzoek voorspelt geen verbetering. Vanuit de manosfeer winnen middeleeuwse denkbeelden van mannen over vrouwen terrein in de klaslokalen en beïnvloeden ze de denkwijze van de volgende generatie tienermannen. Jongens krijgen steevast het beeld voorgeschoteld dat ze sterk en emotieloos moeten zijn. Dat ze superieur zijn aan vrouwen. Dat er geweld mag worden gebruikt.

Politici, ook in dit parlement, bevestigen deze gekte en wij zetten mede daardoor koers naar meer geweld, meer slachtoffers, meer politie‑inzet en overvolle opvang en zorg. Daarom is het belangrijk dat we hier politiek iets tegenover zetten. Met deze richtlijn wordt orde op zaken gesteld. Hiermee wordt de hulp aan slachtoffers overal in Europa beter geregeld en dat is een goede zaak.
Het is nu aan de lidstaten. Neem het welzijn van meer dan de helft van de bevolking serieus.

interventions.speaker_label: Saskia Bricmont, au nom du groupe Verts/ALE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, protéger les victimes, cela semble aller de soi. Et pourtant, ce qui m’a le plus choqué en travaillant sur ce dossier, en rencontrant les associations de victimes et en écoutant les victimes des attentats, notamment de Bruxelles, c’est l’abandon qu’elles ressentent de la part de l’État belge. Nous n’avons pas pu empêcher les attaques mortifères, mais il était de notre responsabilité collective d’accompagner, de protéger et de soutenir les victimes.

Nous avons donc fait en sorte que la directive sur les droits des victimes sur laquelle nous allons voter cette semaine renforce leur soutien, leur protection et leur accès à la justice. Nous avons fait en sorte que les victimes ou des tiers puissent adresser un signalement de manière sûre, que la protection contre la victimisation secondaire soit renforcée et qu’il y ait une meilleure prise en compte des discriminations.

Mais pour que ces nouvelles assurances soient efficaces, c’est sur la réelle volonté politique de nos États, responsables de leur mise en œuvre, que les victimes vont devoir compter. Plus de moyens, plus de ressources sont nécessaires; les besoins sont importants. La Commission européenne aura aussi le rôle de vigie pour que les États et nos gouvernements mettent tout en place afin que, plus jamais, une seule victime ne se sente abandonnée.

Η πραγματική δοκιμασία, κατά τη γνώμη μου, είναι η εφαρμογή της, και θα σας πω γιατί. Στην πατρίδα μου είδαμε ακριβώς το αντίθετο από ό, τι συζητάμε σήμερα. Η Κυριακή Γρίβα, θύμα γυναικοκτονίας έξω από αστυνομικό τμήμα, πήγε να ζητήσει βοήθεια και τα αστυνομικά όργανα είπαν «το περιπολικό δεν είναι ταξί» και δολοφονήθηκε έξω από το αστυνομικό τμήμα. Βεβαίως εδώ πρέπει να πούμε ότι έχουμε πολλές περιπτώσεις γυναικών που πέφτουν θύματα γυναικοκτονίας. Αυτή είναι η πλήρης αποτυχία ενός συστήματος που δεν ακούει τα θύματα και εκ των υστέρων εκδίδει ανακοινώσεις θλίψης και συμπόνοιας. Νομίζω, κύριε Επίτροπε, αυτή η οδηγία είναι μια θετική αρχή.

interventions.speaker_label: Mary Khan, im Namen der ESN-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Ein 15-jähriges Mädchen wurde in Hamburg Opfer einer Gruppenvergewaltigung. Bis heute ist sie traumatisiert. Elf Männer standen vor Gericht, nur einer kam ins Gefängnis. Sie wurde von diesem System im Stich gelassen, von jenem System, das durch die illegale Masseneinwanderung auch das Phänomen der Gruppenvergewaltigung importiert hat – auch wenn die SPD das nach wie vor leugnet.

Und dann das Unfassbare: Eine Frau schreibt aus Empörung einen sogenannten Hasskommentar gegen einen der Täter und landet im Arrest. Der verurteilte Vergewaltiger bleibt draußen. Das ist kein Opferschutz! Und zu Opferschutz gehört auch Gerechtigkeit für die Eltern. Seit 2015 werden immer mehr migrantische Täter als schuldunfähig erklärt. Die Mutter von Liana K. und die Eltern vom ermordeten Yannis aus Aschaffenburg werden niemals Gerechtigkeit erfahren, denn die Mörder werden wegen angeblicher Kriegstraumata als unzurechnungsfähig eingestuft – das neue Lieblingsframing der Linken.
Das fehlt uns in diesem Entwurf und deswegen werden wir nicht dafür stimmen.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, costruire uno spazio di libertà, sicurezza e giustizia significa prevenire i reati e punirne gli autori, certo, ma significa anche assicurare giustizia a quei 75 milioni di persone che ogni anno, nell'Unione europea, sono vittime di criminalità.

Assicurare giustizia alle vittime vuol dire fornire loro assistenza, supporto e protezione adeguati alle loro specifiche esigenze, anche per incoraggiarle a denunciare e impedire così che i reati, soprattutto quelli più violenti, restino impuniti.

E, ancora, significa riconoscere i loro diritti in tutto il corso del procedimento e garantirne l'esercizio concreto anche nei casi transfrontalieri, proteggere la loro riservatezza e tutelare la loro dignità impedendo fenomeni di vittimizzazione secondaria.

Chi, come me – consentitemi una nota personale – ha purtroppo vissuto la drammatica esperienza di vittima o, più specificamente, familiare di una vittima di un gravissimo reato – l'uccisione di mio padre da parte della criminalità organizzata mafiosa – conosce la sofferenza delle vittime e sa bene quanto tutto ciò sia importante.

Piena approvazione, quindi, per la nuova direttiva, che armonizza e rafforza in tutta l'Unione i servizi, le garanzie e i diritti per le vittime di reato, in particolare le più vulnerabili, come donne, minori e persone con disabilità, istituendo una linea di supporto comune e garantendo l'assistenza legale alle vittime in stato di bisogno.

Per questo, ringrazio i relatori e rivolgo alla Commissione un invito a monitorare attentamente l'attuazione delle nuove disposizioni, perché il processo è davvero giusto solo se anche alla vittima viene riconosciuta e assicurata giustizia.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, thank you to the rapporteurs, Lucia Yar and Javier Zarzalejos, because today we mark the most significant reform of EU victim protection in over a decade, and a very important one for women and girls, because behind this directive, there are numbers that should shake us. One in three European women has faced violence and one in six has survived sexual violence. Yet the vast majority do not report because they want to avoid re-victimisation, because they do not trust in institutions or in justice, or because they think no one will believe them.

But we are here to change that and we will go on pushing for a European consent-based rape legislation. But for now we are breaking down the walls of fear by guaranteeing safer reporting, EU-wide helplines and free trauma-informed psychological support. Crucial for our committee, the FEMM Committee, is to ensure that for survivors of rape, access to information on sexual and reproductive healthcare, including abortion care, is explicitly addressed in this directive. Thank you very much for continuing to work for the victims.

One in three European women has faced violence and one in six has survived sexual violence. Yet the vast majority do not report because they want to avoid re-victimisation, because they do not trust in institutions or in justice, or because they think no one will believe them.

But we are here to change that and we will go on pushing for a European consent-based rape legislation. But for now we are breaking down the walls of fear by guaranteeing safer reporting, EU-wide helplines and free trauma-informed psychological support. Crucial for our committee, the FEMM Committee, is to ensure that for survivors of rape, access to information on sexual and reproductive healthcare, including abortion care, is explicitly addressed in this directive. Thank you very much for continuing to work for the victims.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Für uns hat der Schutz von Kriminalitätsopfern natürlich höchste Priorität. Doch obwohl es einige positive Aspekte hier gibt, spare ich nicht an Kritik.

Vor allem wird wieder einmal ein Text vorgelegt, in dem eine stark ideologisierte Sprache vorherrscht. Schauen wir uns Begriffe an wie intersectional discrimination und gender identity, dann ebenso die Einbindung von NGOs in Machtpositionen und die Verknüpfung mit sexueller und reproduktiver Gesundheit – die haben in einer Opferrichtlinie absolut nichts verloren!

An der nächsten Stelle: Brutale Messerattacken, schon angesprochen von meiner Kollegin, Gruppenvergewaltigungen und Überfälle auf unsere Bürger sind keine Einzelfälle mehr. Sie sind das direkte Ergebnis einer verfehlten EU-Migrationspolitik mit offenen Grenzen und weichgespülten Gesetzen. Die Täter werden oft nur milde bestraft, schnell wieder freigelassen oder gar nicht erst abgeschoben.

Es geht also darum, den Opferschutz in den Vordergrund zu stellen, nicht, wie es hier wieder einmal passiert, auch das nationale Strafrecht der einzelnen Mitgliedstaaten hintanzustellen, was eine klare Kompetenzüberschreitung der EU darstellt.
Wir wollen ein Europa, das seine Bürger schützt und nicht ideologisch missbraucht.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, que de temps perdu, que de temps perdu! La directive sur le droit des victimes, prévue comme un texte de bon sens, en première lecture dans cet hémicycle, a été retardée par la gauche et le centre, plus obsédés par la mention de l'avortement que par le soutien efficace et rapide aux victimes. Or, le premier droit des victimes, c'est la réparation. Et la réparation passe par la sanction.

Protéger les victimes, c'est d'abord l'affaire des nations. Protéger les victimes, c'est infliger des peines exemplaires et en finir avec le laxisme judiciaire, notamment en France. Protéger les victimes, c'est avoir une politique carcérale digne de ce nom, qui évite aux victimes de recroiser leurs agresseurs, parfois très peu de temps après les faits. Protéger les victimes, c'est en finir avec la culture de l'excuse et de l'impunité pour les voleurs, les violeurs et les casseurs. Protéger les victimes, enfin, c'est arrêter d'importer des prédateurs sur notre sol, notamment par le biais de l'immigration.

paragraphs.text: Gospa predsednica, ta direktiva je pomemben korak naprej, ker končno krepi zaščito žrtev, dostop do psihološke pomoči, zaščito zasebnosti in preprečevanje sekundarne viktimizacije – ponovila bom – končno.

Ampak žal moram povedati še nekaj. Nekateri v tej dvorani zelo radi govorijo o zaščiti žrtev, dokler žrtev ne zahteva tudi avtonomije, lastne pravice, lastne odločitve, lastnega življenja po nasilju, po posilstvu.

Takrat smo pa nenadoma spet pri ideologiji in političnih interpretacijah pravic. Ali veste – ne morete govoriti o dostojanstvu žrtev, če ženskam po travmi ne zaupate niti toliko, da same odločajo o svojem življenju.
Ker se sekundarna viktimizacije ne dogaja samo na policijskih postajah ali sodiščih. Včasih se dogaja tudi tukaj, ko se travmo žrtev spreminja v ideološko bojišče.
Kolegice, kolegi. Evropska unija ne sme biti prostor, kjer se žrtve bojijo sistema bolj kot storilca. Žrtev ne zaščitimo z moraliziranjem. Zaščitimo jih tako, da jim verjamemo. Hvala.

paragraphs.text: Fru talman! En kvinna blir slagen i ett förhållande, flyr, söker hjälp och finner trygghet på ett skyddat boende. Sveriges kvinnorörelser har under decennier byggt upp dessa trygga rum för kvinnor i nöd.

Mäns våld fortsätter, men nu stängs de skyddade boendena ner, ett efter ett. Varje år dödas femton kvinnor av en man i Sverige. I EU är siffrorna runt 2 600 kvinnor. Jag hoppas att det här förslaget stoppar den utvecklingen.

För i Sverige, ett land med tydliga jämställdhetsmål, fortsätter våldet. Den svenska regeringen säger att de ska göra mer för kvinnor än någon annan regering tidigare gjort. Samtidigt som rum efter rum för kvinnofrid stängs ner och kvinnorörelsen utarmas.

Skyddade boenden skyddar kvinnors liv. De måste få vara kvar. Varje stängt boende är en förlorad chans till kvinnofrid. Och jag välkomnar att denna nya lagstiftning sätter press även på den svenska regeringen att gå från ord till handling.

paragraphs.text: Vážená pani predsedajúca. Kvôli vám – progresívcom, ktorí predkladáte toto nariadenie, sú na dennej báze v Európe vraždení nevinní ľudia, znásilňované ženy. Aj napriek tomu, že sa teraz usmievate od ucha k uchu, je to práve kvôli vám, že sú tu deti unášané na dennej báze a že sexuálne násilie takto vystrelilo do nebies. Všetky grafy, všetky fakty poukazujú na to, že západná Európa je plná vrahov, násilníkov a teroristov, ktorí tu nemajú čo robiť. Ale namiesto toho, aby ste jasne povedali: poďme toto zlo z našich ulíc deportovať preč, poďme poslať týchto kriminálnikov a vrahov tam, odkiaľ prišli, tak prídete s nariadením, kde priamo pomenúvate nelegálnych imigrantov ako iregulárnych imigrantov, ako nejakých nie bežných ľudí, čím legalizujete zlo, ktoré v našich uliciach nemá čo robiť. A dokonca žiadate pre väčšie práva pre týchto nelegálnych imigrantov, lebo čo ak sa im vraj dejú v nejakých táboroch krivdy. To je choré a zvrátené. Vy, progresívci, máte celé ruky od krvi nevinných obetí a treba vás konečne zastaviť.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, de trop nombreuses victimes vivent une double peine. D'abord l'agression, puis l'épreuve du parcours judiciaire: procédure interminable, soutien psychologique insuffisant, indemnisation inégale. Une victime n'est pas un dossier administratif; c'est un être humain qui a besoin de protection, d'écoute et de reconstruction.

Aussi, je salue le travail effectué, car nous reconnaissons enfin les victimes comme de véritables acteurs du processus judiciaire et non simplement des témoins. Nous proposons un socle européen qui comprend de véritables outils: accompagnement juridique, aide psychologique, protection renforcée des publics vulnérables. La sécurité ne se mesure pas uniquement au nombre d'arrestations et de condamnations; elle se mesure également à notre capacité à reconstruire les victimes.

Mais nous devons également réfléchir à l'imprescriptibilité de certains crimes. Une démocratie digne de ce nom ne doit en effet jamais donner le sentiment que le temps protège davantage le criminel que la victime.

paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, Г-н Комисар, колеги, в законодателството няма място за емоции, но когато става въпрос за ревизия на Директивата за правата на жертвите на престъпления, зад всеки текст стоят човешки съдби.
По професия съм адвокат и през годините съм се сблъсквал с различни казуси. Знам, че човешката болка говори много повече и от най-стряскащата статистика.
Днес все по-често жертвите не викат за помощ на улицата. Те мълчат зад екраните.
Дигиталното пространство създава илюзия, че насилието не е истинско, но последствията са напълно реални.
А освен дигитален, все повече престъпления имат и трансграничен характер. Европа трябва да гарантира, че независимо къде се намира една жертва, тя ще получи защита, информация и достъп до правосъдие.

Но по-добра подкрепа за жертвите означава и по-добре подготвени институции. Нуждаем се от обучени съдии, прокурори, полицейски служители и всички професионалисти, които работят с жертви на престъпления. Нуждаем се от по-модерни и дигитализирани системи за правосъдие, които улесняват достъпа до информация и защитата на правата на гражданите.

И тук е важна ролята на европейски инструменти като програма „Правосъдие“. Инвестициите в обучение, цифровизация и трансграничното сътрудничество превръщат принципите в реален капацитет за защита на хората.

Не можем да допускаме жертвите, независимо дали става въпрос за онлайн тормоз, измами, трафик, домашно насилие или сексуална експлоатация, да бъдат повторно травматизирани от самата система. Тя трябва да гарантира подкрепа. Доверието в правосъдието започва от отношението към жертвите.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Schwer traumatisiert bewältigen sie ihren mühevollen Alltag und finden doch keine Ruhe. Die Rede ist von Überlebenden schwerer Straftaten. Allzu oft werden sie mit den physischen, psychischen und finanziellen Folgen allein gelassen. Und immer wieder werden sie sogar direkt von Tätern kontaktiert. Unangekündigt. Unerwartet. Legal? Leider ja. Und das wird so bleiben, wenn wir jetzt nicht handeln.

Mit der Abstimmung morgen setzen wir den Fokus auf die Bedürfnisse der Opfer. Wir schließen Schutzlücken, schützen persönliche Daten der Opfer vor dem Zugriff der Täter. Wir erleichtern den Zugang zu Beratung, Betreuung, Unterstützung und Entschädigung. Wir sorgen für bessere Sensibilisierung von Richterinnen, Polizistinnen und anderen. Und dieser Schutz soll gelten, unabhängig davon, wo in der EU ein Mensch Opfer einer Straftat wurde, damit Betroffene nicht noch mehr Leid ertragen müssen als bereits bei der Tat selbst.

Und Kolleginnen und Kollegen, wenn ich hier im Hause hören muss, dass Gewalt nur existiert, weil es Migration gibt, dann ist das ein Schlag ins Gesicht aller Opfer. Und ich möchte mich bei allen Opfern für solche Aussagen entschuldigen.
(Die Rednerin lehnt Fragen nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ von Lukas Sieper und Arkadiusz Mularczyk ab.)

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I welcome the agreement on the Victims' Rights Directive and it is a step forward in justice. But let us be very honest, we have a long way to go.

While justice must always be seen to be done, it is adversarial. It can be very hostile to victims of crime, and very often the onus is on the victim beyond their capacity in presenting a case. And that makes it difficult, particularly in the areas of coercion, domestic violence and sexual violence. So while we have this framework in place, we do need to ensure that across Member States there is a sea change around the issue of domestic violence and coercion.

We recently saw a case in Ireland that was a tragic case with regard to Nicola Hanney, who made a complaint to the Garda Ombudsman, and yet there was very little action taken. And if we want action taken, we do need to ensure that the authorities and those agencies that are charged with the responsibility of investigation, they must build trust among the broader public. So victims will have confidence to go there in the first place.

On the issue in Ireland, for example, it is estimated that only 5 % of adults who have experienced sexual violence reported to the police ‑ only 5 %. We have a long way to go. This is a step, but we have many steps to take.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, Celeste ha 12 anni e ha visto molte volte il padre picchiare la madre. Fa fatica a dormire e a concentrarsi e tende a isolarsi.

I bambini sono vittime di violenza domestica sia quando sono colpiti direttamente sia quando assistono alla violenza contro un genitore. Quest'ultima viene chiamata "violenza assistita", ma è violenza e basta.

In Italia, gli ultimi dati Istat mostrano che quasi otto figli su dieci assistono alla violenza subita dalla madre, bambini che crescono nella paura, nell'iperallerta e nel senso di colpa, che sviluppano ansia, depressione o aggressività.

Per questo, la revisione della direttiva "Vittime" segna un passo importante: riconosce finalmente servizi di assistenza e protezione specifici per i minori testimoni di reato e per gli orfani di femminicidio, così da prevenire una seconda traumatizzazione attraverso servizi integrati, coordinati e accessibili nello stesso luogo.

Il principio guida è sancito all'articolo 24 della nostra Carta dei diritti fondamentali, la preminenza dell'interesse superiore del minore, perché una comunità davvero accudente riconosce che tutelare i bambini significa fare prevenzione, evitare danni sul loro sviluppo e spezzare la trasmissione intergenerazionale della violenza.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, around 50 million women in the European Union, nearly one in three, have experienced physical or sexual violence in adulthood. 50 million – these are not numbers on a page, they are lives marked by fear, trauma and injustice. And for too many women, the fight does not end with escaping violence, it continues in systems that question them instead of protecting them. This is unacceptable. That is why the Victims' Rights Directive matters. Strengthening victims' rights is not charity, and it's not bureaucracy either, it is our responsibility.

As former rapporteur for the gender-based violence directive and the rapporteur for the Parliament's report calling for EU consent-based rape legislation, I strongly welcome the stronger protections, better support services and improved access to justice secured in this agreement. These are not technical measures, they are lifelines because one principle must always guide us: women's rights and victims' rights cannot depend on where you live in the European Union – justice must know no borders.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, it's hard to believe that I and others are still standing here arguing for basic protections for victims of crime across Europe in 2026, and the last EU Victims Law was written in 2012. Since then, crime has gone digital, abuse has gone cross-borders, and parts of the online world have become a breeding ground for harassment, exploitation and intimidation, particularly targeting women and young people. And unfortunately, Europe hasn't kept up.
So right now, victims still face different levels of protection depending on which country they are in, while criminals are exploiting our borders and victims shouldn't suffer because of this.
So the crime does not stop with the borders. So therefore the victims' rights shouldn't stop there either.

And let's be honest, for many victims, the trauma does not end when or where the crime happens, because for too many, and particularly of our women, they are forced to face and fight through our national systems because of delays and needless bureaucracy. And all they want to do is either just be heard or protected.
In Ireland, we saw the devastating consequences of online abuse through the tragic death of Nicole 'Coco' Fox, which then led to Coco's Law.

For years we have been pushing for these protections to be recognised across Europe. And I really hope that the report that we are voting on here this week is a first step to that realisation of a European Coco's Law, because victims do not need us to continue talking, they do not need more delays. They need Europe to act and finally deliver on the protections that match the reality of the world that we live in today, unfortunately.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, questa settimana il Parlamento europeo sta marcando un passo importante.

La direttiva su diritti, assistenza e protezione delle vittime di reato mette al centro le persone: minori che hanno vissuto l'orrore degli abusi, vittime della tratta di esseri umani, donne e uomini che portano il peso dell'odio online e della violenza; persone che, oltre al trauma, affrontano il silenzio e l'indifferenza della società e delle istituzioni che dovrebbero invece proteggerle.

Le donne sono tra le più colpite: ci sono le vittime di violenza domestica, odio online, stalking, stupro. Loro, in particolare, spesso si trovano a subire una seconda ingiustizia quando, cercando di denunciare, vengono lasciate sole o addirittura colpevolizzate.

Per questo, cogliamo con favore i progressi significativi contenuti nella direttiva: traguardi come il potenziamento del supporto psicologico, il sostegno alle infrastrutture come i centri antiviolenza e la tutela della privacy delle vittime sono solo alcuni dei passi fondamentali.

Celebriamo anche un altro traguardo: per la prima volta l'accesso alla salute sessuale e riproduttiva, incluso l'aborto sicuro e legale, è riconosciuto come parte dell'assistenza alle vittime di reato.
L'Europa è credibile solo quando protegge i più vulnerabili, senza lasciare indietro nessuno. Con questo voto, mandiamo un messaggio chiaro: in Europa nessuna vittima può sentirsi sola.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario McGrath, por fin celebramos en este Parlamento Europeo la conclusión de la negociación con el Consejo, que pone punto final a un procedimiento legislativo de actualización de la Directiva por la que se establecen normas mínimas sobre los derechos, el apoyo y la protección de las víctimas de delitos, aprobada en 2011 y que conseguimos completar en la pasada legislatura, en la que me impliqué intensamente en la Comisión de Libertades Civiles, Justicia y Asuntos de Interior.

Pero no ha sido hasta esta legislatura cuando por fin se ha completado este procedimiento legislativo, evitando la doble victimización de quienes han sido víctimas del delito, reforzando su asistencia jurídica y procesal, su asistencia social y hasta psicológica, y, particularmente, poniendo la mirada en las personas más vulnerables. Estas son, por supuesto, los menores y los niños víctimas de delitos, pero también las mujeres, que son doblemente victimizadas, particularmente cuando han sido víctimas de violencia sexual y requieren una atención muy especial en sus derechos sexuales y reproductivos, donde el Grupo S&D ha puesto el acento. También lo son los migrantes. Por eso se facilita a las personas más vulnerables el derecho a la denuncia incluso cuando se encuentran en centros de retención o privadas de libertad.
Por ello, solo puedo concluir que los derechos de las víctimas son más derechos humanos que nunca en la ley europea como consecuencia de este procedimiento legislativo.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I very much welcome this debate on the rights, supports and protection of victims of crime. And I want to focus on one group of victims of crime in particular, and that is victims of drug debt, intimidation and drug-debt enforcement. They are a group that are increasingly prevalent, unfortunately, in the constituency which I represent ‑ Ireland South ‑ and they are increasingly prevalent across all of Ireland, and I believe it cannot be a problem that is unique to Ireland.

As drug use increases across Ireland and across the European Union so too does drug debt and so too does drug enforcement. These are often young men, but young people who are afraid to seek help, they are told, don't go to the Gardaí. Don't go to the police force. Don't go to police authorities and they don't, because they don't believe that they will receive protection.

And I spoke to one former constituency colleague of mine who would have served in Dáil Éireann with both of us, Commissioner, and he said he has been to many funerals of young men who have taken their lives now because they see no alternative, they see no way out.
Simply put, we do need to find a way to instil confidence in people that they will receive protection. We do need to address this at national level and at European level.

They are a group that are increasingly prevalent, unfortunately, in the constituency which I represent ‑ Ireland South ‑ and they are increasingly prevalent across all of Ireland, and I believe it cannot be a problem that is unique to Ireland.

As drug use increases across Ireland and across the European Union so too does drug debt and so too does drug enforcement. These are often young men, but young people who are afraid to seek help, they are told, don't go to the Gardaí. Don't go to the police force. Don't go to police authorities and they don't, because they don't believe that they will receive protection.

And I spoke to one former constituency colleague of mine who would have served in Dáil Éireann with both of us, Commissioner, and he said he has been to many funerals of young men who have taken their lives now because they see no alternative, they see no way out.

Simply put, we do need to find a way to instil confidence in people that they will receive protection. We do need to address this at national level and at European level.

Molaim na cearta seo, mar cabhraíonn sé le híospartaigh, an ceart a fháil in am agus i slite praiticiúla.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Mr Commissioner, imagine you are a victim of a crime, or a relative is a victim of a crime. And then you see your face, your name on posters and social media posts and demonstrations here in Parliament, in speeches, used as a pawn for political gains over and over again. And you have to first live through all of that, what you suffered, over and over again because you're reminded about it through the media. Also, maybe you don't even agree with the political actors that use your face, your name, your story.

I believe, if we think about the protection of victims of crime, we should also think about the development of the concept of the right to identity, and if we want to stop people being used as pawns in political communication against their will.

interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, my thanks to all of the honourable Members who contributed to the debate here this evening. Thank you for putting victims at the centre of the debate tonight, and in particular the most vulnerable victims of crime in the European Union, including women, children and other groups who are very vulnerable.

Our message is abundantly clear: the revised directive represents a fundamental shift from minimum standards to tangible, meaningful protection for the most vulnerable among us, including where such victims are children. It ensures that they will be able to see that justice is done for them. A criminal justice system that supports and protects victims of crime is essential, but is not on its own sufficient, as we know, to uphold their rights. We must foster societies where victims' needs and rights are deeply embedded within resilient communities and robust democracies. To achieve this we need strong institutional structures, adequate resources and unwavering commitment to victims of crime, especially to mitigate the impact of future economic or social crises.

The revised directive and the forthcoming strategy are the tools we need to meet these challenges and, crucially, as colleagues will know, we need also to secure sufficient EU funding to support these priorities under the next multiannual financial framework. The Commission's proposal for a new justice programme in the new MFF is ambitious, and I think is worthy of support.

I would also highlight the digitalisation of justice strategy that we have adopted, and also the European judicial training strategy, because it is crucial that, when victims of crime come into contact with a court in a Member State, they are given access to justice and the support that they need at that point in time. We count on Parliament's support to preserve the ambition of the Commission's proposal in the context of the MFF, and ultimately, no victim of crime in the Union should be denied their rights or the support that they need to recover from the harm that has been suffered.

A number of colleagues tonight have spoken about the importance of victims of crime having the confidence in the system and having the trust in the system that they will receive support, that they will receive an adequate level of protection from the criminal justice system, and fundamentally, that they will secure justice itself for the crime that has been perpetrated on them. I want to assure you that once the Council and this Parliament have adopted the legislation, we will ensure that full support is provided to the Member States for the transposition of this directive. We will have a very sharp focus on implementation because, as many of you have rightly said this evening, what is written in the law itself is not meaningful unless it is worked out in practice and is the lived reality of victims of crime in the European Union.

In parallel, I want to assure you that the Commission will ensure coherent transposition of complementary victims' rights provisions stemming from recent sectoral legislation, such as the directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence.

Thank you for your contributions this evening. I think collectively we have done good work on behalf of victims of crime in the European Union. The next step following the formal adoption is to make sure that this is implemented in reality, and that the lived experience of the millions of victims of crime in the European Union is actually improved, and that they get the support and the protection that they need, and that they get access to the justice that they deserve in the Member States of the EU.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Komisarzu! Na koniec dostanie Pan ode mnie najtrudniejsze pytanie w całej tej debacie. Bo dziś, gdy mówimy o prawie ofiar – prawie do godności, równości, do odszkodowania – musimy po raz kolejny upomnieć się o prawo ofiar II wojny światowej – żyjących jeszcze ofiar w Polsce, w Grecji i innych krajach Unii Europejskiej, które wciąż nie mają prawa do sądu, wciąż nie mają prawa do odszkodowania i wciąż są po raz kolejny wiktymizowane.

W Polsce żyje około 50 tysięcy ludzi w podeszłym wieku, które nie dostały nigdy żadnego odszkodowania od państwa niemieckiego za skutki wojny – skutki kalectwa, skutki ciężkiego uszczerbku na zdrowiu. Z drugiej strony państwo niemieckie nie stać na gest humanitarny wobec żyjących ofiar II wojny światowej. Unia Europejska nie dostrzega tego problemu, uznając, że brak prawa do odszkodowania dla ofiar II wojny światowej nie stanowi problemu dla Unii Europejskiej. Panie Komisarzu, bardzo Pana proszę o podjęcie interwencji w tej sprawie. Nie może być tak, że wykluczamy dużą grupę obywateli Unii...

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, muchas gracias a todos los diputados que han participado en este debate, a los que apoyan nuestra propuesta y a los que han criticado esta Directiva.

Lamento, sin embargo, que algunos de nuestros estimados diputados hayan hablado más de los delincuentes que de las víctimas y lamento también que se hable de imposición ideológica, porque creo que no hace justicia al trabajo que se ha realizado.
¿Qué hay de imposición ideológica en que las víctimas tengan derecho a la protección frente a la glorificación del delito?

¿Qué hay de imposición ideológica en que las víctimas sean informadas en el proceso, que se proteja su identidad, que se asegure la asistencia legal, el derecho a recurrir decisiones judiciales que les afectan, el derecho a ser escuchadas?
¿Qué imposición ideológica hay en que se integren servicios especializados, en que se establezcan líneas de ayuda y que se facilite la denuncia?
¿Qué imposición ideológica hay en identificar aquellos grupos de víctimas más vulnerables, con necesidades especiales, y hacia las cuales nosotros tenemos la obligación de ofrecer apoyo especial?

¿Qué imposición ideológica hay en afirmar, de manera estricta y clara, la competencia nacional sobre los servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva que pueden ser ofrecidos a las mujeres víctimas de violencia sexual?

No, no hay imposición ideológica. Esta es una Directiva que ha nacido, que se ha desarrollado y que se ha podido culminar en medio del espíritu de consenso y presidida por él. Y ese espíritu de consenso nos permite hoy ofrecer un importante paso adelante en la protección de las víctimas.

Agradezco a los grupos y a las asociaciones de víctimas con los que nos hemos entrevistado. También, por supuesto, expreso mi agradecimiento a la coponente Lucia Yar y a todos los que han participado, específicamente al comisario McGrath y a sus servicios, por el apoyo que nos han prestado y por su compromiso personal para hacer posible hoy que mañana podamos reunir el máximo apoyo a esta Directiva.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, thank you for this debate, but I must address the attempts to really turn the victims suffering into some kind of cheap ideological battleground.

You from the far right, stop using women's suffering for cheap political points. It's enough. Once again, you have been bluntly lying here, pushing the idea that the violence against women somehow comes from outside or from other cultures. But the facts are pretty uncomfortable for you, right? But they matter. In Europe, women are most often harmed, abused and killed by men they know: their partners, ex-partners or family members. So the biggest threat to a woman is not a stranger crossing a border – it is violence behind closed doors. So please have some dignity and respect for victims.

In order to finish on a positive note – because this was a really difficult negotiation, and we reached a very, very good result – I would like to thank Commissioner McGrath, especially, for taking this directive very seriously and continuously having victims and the most vulnerable people in the centre of his attention. I would also like to thank the Council, especially the Polish and Danish presidencies, who helped to advance the whole legislation further.

I would also like to thank my co‑rapporteur, Mr Javier Zarzalejos, Lina Gálvez, also colleagues, shadow rapporteurs, other colleagues involved, all the advisors and assistants, many, many people who have negotiated this very important law because everyone involved, you should be very much proud of yourselves. You've made victims' rights in the European Union stronger. And tomorrow, together, we are going to make history. Thank you, everybody.

paragraphs.text: Marc Angel (S&D), in writingNo victim of crime should ever feel abandoned, unheard or left alone to navigate the consequences of violence and abuse. This is why the revision of the EU Victims’ Rights Directive is such an important step forward for Europe.The new rules will strengthen the protection and support available to victims across the EU. They aim to make reporting crimes easier, improve access to justice and compensation, and ensure that victims receive timely information and specialised support throughout legal proceedings.This reform matters because justice cannot only be about punishing perpetrators – it must also be about protecting people, restoring dignity and ensuring equal access to support, regardless of income, gender, disability or nationality.A Europe that truly defends fundamental rights is one that listens to victims, believes them and stands beside them.At a time when fear, insecurity and mistrust are growing across our societies, this vote sends another message: solidarity and human rights remain at the heart of the European project.These are the policies that make the EU stronger – when we choose to care for people, protect the vulnerable and act together for dignity, equality and justice across Europe.

paragraphs.text: Έλενα Κουντουρά (The Left), γραπτώςΚυρία Πρόεδρε, κύριοι συνάδελφοι, η αναθεώρηση της οδηγίας για τα δικαιώματα των θυμάτων αποτελεί αναγκαία θεσμική αλλαγή για την ενίσχυση της προστασίας των θυμάτων βίας. Αν και δεν καλύπτει όλα όσα ζητούσαμε, πετύχαμε βελτιώσεις που για χρόνια διεκδικούσαν γυναίκες, οργανώσεις και προοδευτικές πολιτικές δυνάμεις.Στηρίζουμε την ενίσχυση του δικαιώματος στην ιδιωτική ζωή και την προστασία προσωπικών δεδομένων των θυμάτων. Για πρώτη φορά αναγνωρίζεται ξεκάθαρα ότι η αποκάλυψη στοιχείων, όπως η διεύθυνση κατοικίας, μπορεί να θέσει σε κίνδυνο γυναίκες και παιδιά που προσπαθούν να ξεφύγουν από κακοποιητικές καταστάσεις. Αφορά σε πάγια διεκδίκησή μου για τη στήριξη των θυμάτων ενδοοικογενειακής βίας, ως εισηγήτρια του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου στην έκθεση-ψήφισμα του 2021 για τον «αντίκτυπο της ενδοσυντροφικής βίας και των δικαιωμάτων επιμέλειας στις γυναίκες και τα παιδιά».Θετικό βήμα είναι η υποχρεωτική εκπαίδευση των αρχών και υπηρεσιών για την αποτροπή της δευτερογενούς θυματοποίησης, η καθιέρωση διαδικασιών πιο φιλικών προς το παιδί θύμα και η βελτιωμένη πρόσβαση των θυμάτων σε ψηφιακούς μηχανισμούς καταγγελίας, νομική και ψυχολογική βοήθεια και εξειδικευμένες υπηρεσίες υποστήριξης. Σε μία περίοδο αμφισβήτησης των σεξουαλικών και αναπαραγωγικών δικαιωμάτων, είναι σημαντικό πολιτικά ότι για πρώτη φορά ευρωπαϊκή οδηγία αναγνωρίζει, έστω σε αιτιολογική σκέψη, την πρόσβαση σε υπηρεσίες άμβλωσης για θύματα σεξουαλικής βίας, όπου προβλέπεται από το εθνικό δίκαιο.

Αφορά σε πάγια διεκδίκησή μου για τη στήριξη των θυμάτων ενδοοικογενειακής βίας, ως εισηγήτρια του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου στην έκθεση-ψήφισμα του 2021 για τον «αντίκτυπο της ενδοσυντροφικής βίας και των δικαιωμάτων επιμέλειας στις γυναίκες και τα παιδιά».Θετικό βήμα είναι η υποχρεωτική εκπαίδευση των αρχών και υπηρεσιών για την αποτροπή της δευτερογενούς θυματοποίησης, η καθιέρωση διαδικασιών πιο φιλικών προς το παιδί θύμα και η βελτιωμένη πρόσβαση των θυμάτων σε ψηφιακούς μηχανισμούς καταγγελίας, νομική και ψυχολογική βοήθεια και εξειδικευμένες υπηρεσίες υποστήριξης. Σε μία περίοδο αμφισβήτησης των σεξουαλικών και αναπαραγωγικών δικαιωμάτων, είναι σημαντικό πολιτικά ότι για πρώτη φορά ευρωπαϊκή οδηγία αναγνωρίζει, έστω σε αιτιολογική σκέψη, την πρόσβαση σε υπηρεσίες άμβλωσης για θύματα σεξουαλικής βίας, όπου προβλέπεται από το εθνικό δίκαιο.

paragraphs.text: Jagna Marczułajtis-Walczak (PPE), na piśmieKażdego roku miliony osób w Unii Europejskiej doświadczają przemocy, wykorzystywania i innych przestępstw, często pozostając bez odpowiedniego wsparcia psychologicznego, prawnego i finansowego.Ta regulacja stanowi ważny krok w kierunku bardziej sprawiedliwego i empatycznego systemu ochrony ofiar, w szczególności dzieci, ofiar przemocy seksualnej oraz osób szczególnie na przemoc narażonych.Zapewnienie łatwiejszego dostępu do pomocy, możliwości zgłaszania przestępstw online, wsparcia psychologicznego i prawnego oraz utworzenie ogólnounijnej infolinii dla ofiar to działania konieczne by zapewnić minimum poczucia bezpieczeństwa.Dlatego teraz wzywamy państwa członkowskie do zapewnienia odpowiednich środków finansowych i kadrowych na skuteczne wdrażanie nowych przepisów oraz do zagwarantowania ofiarom bezpiecznego, godnego i niedyskryminującego dostępu do wymiaru sprawiedliwości i usług wsparcia.Prawa ofiar muszą pozostawać w centrum europejskiego systemu sprawiedliwości.

paragraphs.text: The next item is the debate on a Commission statement on the recruitment of children by organised crime (2026/2725(RSP)).

interventions.text: The next item is the debate on a Commission statement on the recruitment of children by organised crime (2026/2725(RSP)).

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, every child has the fundamental right to be protected. The right to a life free of violence and crime. Criminal networks increasingly target and exploit children, not only as victims of crime, but also to carry out illegal activities.
More and more recruitment is taking place online. Artificial intelligence and digital platforms are transforming the way criminals identify, recruit and also control victims.
Exploitation is becoming more widespread and at the same time is becoming more difficult to detect.

Criminals lure youngsters with promises of easy money, often presenting illegal acts as games or online challenges. Recruiters then move conversations to encrypted messaging channels to give further instructions to minors. Offers can range from a few euros for a courier service to thousands of euros for carrying out a murder. Criminal groups don't just pay, they use intimidation, violence or drugs to trap children. They also groom children to become recruiters themselves, giving them a false sense of belonging.

Children can therefore be victims, forced perpetrators or very often both at the same time. In October 2024, in Marseille, a criminal hired two boys, 14 and 15 years old, via social media to burn rival's houses and even to kill a rival. The 14 year old ended up killing an innocent taxi driver. The 15 year old was stabbed and burned alive by rival gangs before he could commit the arson that he was hired for.

In another case, Spanish authorities arrested criminals who had recruited Swedish youngsters to commit killings in Denmark. This is a very, very serious problem and this is clearly a European problem and it requires a European response.

Strengthening the protection of children is a priority for the European Commission, just as I know it is for you here in the European Parliament. And a lot of measures are already underway. In the 2025 state of the Union address, President van der Leyen underlined her commitment to protecting minors online and announced a special panel on child safety online. The Digital Services Act requires online platforms to protect all users, and especially children, when using their services.

In March this year, the Commission opened a formal investigation into Snapchat over concerns related to the recruitment of minors for criminal purposes. The Commission has also prepared ambitious guidelines for online platforms on the protection of minors, including measures on content moderation and user support.

And less than a month ago, the Commission adopted a recommendation on a European age verification blueprint to encourage Member States to ensure that all EU citizens have access to robust and privacy-preserving age verification by the end of this year. Effective age assurance measures will help providers reduce the risk of minors being exposed to harmful practices that undermine their privacy, or to threaten their very safety and security.

The EU Social Package, adopted just two weeks ago, will help reduce the number of structurally vulnerable children with a strengthened child guarantee and measures to fight poverty and social exclusion.

The EU Internet Forum has brought together law enforcement authorities and companies to identify the terms and emojis frequently used to recruit youngsters online. This forum is also working on detecting harmful materials in games. EU agencies are involved too. The EU Drugs Agency is conducting studies on drug related violence in the EU, and on effective interventions to prevent youth recruitment into illegal drug markets.

Europol, through its Operational Task Force GRIMM, which focuses on the recruitment of children into crime, has developed detection and awareness tools. The task force has already achieved impressive operational results, with 280 arrests made and 14 000 online accounts identified.

So this is a lot, but obviously we know it's not enough. As stressed in the protect EU internal security strategy, protecting children requires a whole of society approach. Protecting children from crime starts with prevention and integrated support. This means investing in education, social inclusion, employment, health care and regional policies. Combating organised crime also means addressing its root causes, preventing violence, offering youngsters credible alternatives to a life of crime and helping them to escape the clutch of gangs.

Later this year, the Commission will present new rules on organised crime to target its ringleaders and key facilitators more effectively. It will also aim to reinforce the penal response against those who recruit children into crime. The Commission will also present a new EU strategy on victims' rights, including on child victims of crime and an action plan on the protection of children against crime.
So thank you for allowing me to set out those opening remarks on this hugely important issue, and I very much look forward to the views of the honourable Members this evening.

interventions.speaker_label: Tomas Tobé, on behalf of the PPE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, cross‑border organised crime now poses a systemic risk to our Union. We are now coming to a situation where criminal networks even recruit children – children – to pull the trigger. This is not business as usual.

Of course, we see that the Commission sees how serious this is, and we do welcome the initiatives. But I do want to underline that we must do more: we need a strong European response, we need to overhaul our legislation at EU level to crack down on the criminal networks and their ruthless operations across our Union. This is not a single issue for the Member States.
My home country, Sweden, is doing a lot, but we know that the criminal networks are active in several Member States at the same time. So we have to have a strong European response.

And here I would like to take the chance to turn to my colleagues on the left: please work together with the EPP to make sure that we can get a strong Europol. And to my colleagues on the right: even if we are talking about a European solution, it doesn't need to be bad.
We have to come together now. We are talking about children that are being exploited by ruthless people, and I think it's time for this House to show that we will not stand for it.

interventions.speaker_label: Sandro Ruotolo, a nome del gruppo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, andando in missione nei porti di Anversa e Rotterdam, abbiamo scoperto la figura degli "estrattori", minori reclutati dalla criminalità organizzata per recuperare la cocaina nei container provenienti dal Sud America. E ho subito pensato alla mia città, Napoli, dove sempre più ragazzi diventano vittime e carnefici di guerre armate.

L'Europa non è l'Eldorado. Oggi, i minori sono coinvolti in oltre il 70 % dei mercati della droga in Europa. Il reclutamento avviene soprattutto online, sui social: le piattaforme digitali sono diventate il nuovo terreno di caccia delle mafie. Europol ha già individuato oltre 14 000 account legati al reclutamento dei minori online.
La risposta non può essere soltanto repressiva. Certo, dobbiamo proteggere i minori nelle piattaforme online, ma la sicurezza si costruisce prima che un ragazzo impugni una pistola.

Sono d'accordo con il Commissario McGrath: dobbiamo servirci della scuola, della cultura, dello sport e dei servizi sociali, perché dove mancano le prospettive di vita, le organizzazioni criminali trovano terreno fertile per loro.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Matthieu Valet, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, je vais vous parler de la France, puisque vous avez parlé de Marseille, Monsieur le Commissaire. Plus 74 % de mineurs poursuivis pour meurtres, assassinats, coups mortels et violences volontaires aggravées entre 2017 et 2023. Un interpellé sur cinq avec une arme est mineur, en France. Près d’un quart des cambriolages impliquent des mineurs. Près d’un tiers des interpellés après les émeutes suite à la mort de Nahel en 2023 étaient également des mineurs. Six mineurs délinquants sur dix récidivent dans les cinq ans après leur condamnation définitive.

Je pense que pour les gauchistes les plus angéliques ou pour celles et ceux qui ne parlent que de prévention, les chiffres sont clairs: il faut d’abord de la répression et une volonté de protéger nos concitoyens qui, eux, ne demandent rien et sont victimes des agissements d’une grande majorité de mineurs qui sont de plus en plus violents.

Alors, des réponses claires? La majorité pénale est à seize ans. Aujourd’hui, elle est à 18 ans. Comment comprendre qu’on juge un mineur de seize ans en 2026 avec des textes de 1945? Ils doivent être jugés comme des majeurs lorsqu’ils commettent des crimes et des délits pour adapter la réponse pénale à la réalité d’aujourd’hui. Les parents démissionnaires qui abandonnent leurs enfants doivent perdre les allocations et le logement social. Et surtout, quand ils cassent, ils doivent payer jusqu’à la fin de leur vie. On veut donc créer une taxe sur les voyous et non pas une taxe sur les victimes.

Alors, la prévention est simple: quand on fait des gosses, on les assume. Aux parents de surveiller les fréquentations, les devoirs, les sorties. Ce n’est que du bon sens. Il faut arrêter la culture de l’excuse sociale et pénale et tout ce qui relève de l’impunité qui nous tue depuis des années.

interventions.speaker_label: Charlie Weimers, on behalf of the ECR Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the ECR Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, child soldiers in Sweden – Sweden, not Africa.

Criminal gangs recruit hitmen as young as 12 years old, lured with promises of watches or designer clothes. Dystopian fiction? Our reality. The direct result of decades of social-democratic failure, mass uncontrolled migration, failed integration and weak punishments.

Europe, you're not immune – Sweden is the canary in the coal mine. Follow the same policies, get the same result: children murdering children. But now the Sweden Democrats and our partners are restoring law and order. Gang crimes, double sentences – violent young offenders, tougher penalties. A child assassin is still an assassin. Why does the left want killers on our streets?

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, commissaris, een paar cijfers: in Antwerpen alleen werden vorig jaar twee keer zoveel minderjarigen aangehouden als het jaar voordien. De jongste was dertien jaar. In Rotterdam en Marseille worden kinderen van acht jaar ingezet als drugskoerier. Dat zijn geen randgevallen. Dit is een structurele crisis. Georganiseerde criminele netwerken rekruteren kinderen op strategische wijze via algoritmen, gamificatie en versleutelde kanalen.

Uit het recente onderzoek van Missing Children Europe weten we nu dat grooming niet alleen een rekruteringstactiek is, maar ook een controlemiddel. Kinderen worden online gegroomd, over de grenzen gesmokkeld, gedwongen tot seksuele handelingen, tot het rekruteren van andere kinderen, tot drugsdistributie.

We moeten drie dingen erkennen. Ten eerste is het rekruteren van kinderen niet alleen een kwestie van kinderbescherming. Het is een interne veiligheidsdreiging en dat moet een centrale pijler worden. Ten tweede bestaat de digitaledienstenverordening, maar algoritmes die kinderen naar criminele netwerken leiden, zijn vandaag nog steeds actief. We moeten meer controleren en handhaven. Ten derde — ik denk dat jullie het er allemaal mee eens zijn — is elk kind dat door een crimineel, een rotzak, gerekruteerd wordt, een slachtoffer en geen dader.
And it is our duty to protect the children.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, de la rue à Anvers, aux quartiers à Marseille ou à Bruxelles, en passant par Snapchat, TikTok, mais aussi Roblox, ces endroits où sont nos enfants et nos ados quotidiennement sont aussi utilisés par les réseaux criminels pour les recruter et pour commettre les pires crimes et activités illégales. Des crimes, des assassinats qui sont perpétrés de plus en plus en Europe. Notre sécurité collective face au crime organisé est en danger, mais c'est celle de nos enfants qui l'est également. Ils sont avant tout des victimes de cette exploitation criminelle, ce qui devrait vraiment réveiller notre conscience collective et nous mobiliser aussi au niveau européen pour contrer efficacement ce phénomène.

Des réponses répressives et sécuritaires ne font malheureusement pas le poids face à l'ampleur de ce problème. Mettre un enfant en prison, c'est assurer que son avenir appartiendra au crime et lui faire perdre l'espoir de tout avenir meilleur. La réponse pénale doit être adaptée et ne suffit pas à elle-même. Le constat est cinglant: là où l'État se désengage, le crime organisé prospère. Amine Kessaci, à Marseille, qui a perdu ses deux frères, ne le sait que trop bien.

Il faut restaurer l'État dans nos villes, nos villages et nos quartiers; réinvestir massivement dans nos écoles et nos services sociaux; éviter les décrochages; prévenir les recrutements par un travail de terrain; réguler les plateformes; aider les victimes et soutenir les équipes de protection de la jeunesse et d'aide à l'enfance qui font un travail incroyable, mais avec des ressources limitées.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, il reclutamento di minori da parte della criminalità organizzata è una piaga per l'intera Europa.
Questi giovanissimi ragazzi vengono sfruttati dalla criminalità per commettere reati di vario genere, traffico di droga, ma anche crimini violenti.

Di fronte a questo allarme non possiamo stare inerti. Servono politiche efficaci a sostegno dei più fragili e azioni decise, coinvolgendo anche le aziende tech sulle cui piattaforme avviene il reclutamento. Serve armonizzare le fattispecie di reato che colpiscono i reclutatori.

La norma sulla criminalità organizzata che verrà presto presentata in questo Parlamento può rappresentare perciò uno strumento essenziale. Occorre una prevenzione efficace, capace di offrire a questi ragazzi valide alternative, ma dobbiamo avere la capacità di arrivare prima che arrivino la magistratura o le forze dell'ordine. Dobbiamo prenderci cura di chi ha avuto la fortuna o la sfortuna di nascere 50 metri prima o 50 metri dopo la periferia di una città.
Questo è il miglior modo di togliere dalle mani della criminalità organizzata i giovani e dare loro speranza.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, their role is drug dealing, ripping off action in harbours, sabotaging, attacking houses, religious sites, objects, sometimes even committing attacks or violent insults against persons, even requests for being a murderer. Their age is on average between 13 and 17, sometimes even younger. Their benefit: money, social benefits, fitting in or being accepted into a certain group. The recruitment tools: peers and, far too often, digital platforms, messengers, the gamification of children's exploitation. The benefits of their recruiters: exploiting minors to avoid detection, prosecution and punishment.

And the outlook – colleagues, let there be no doubt about it – is grim. There is a trend for more violence, more exploitation; the unholy combination of organised crime, radicalised and even terrorist groups and third‑country interests being played out in the European Union. So that's a problem, and I am happy to hear that we agree already on some parts of the solution. So let us act on that: strengthening law enforcement, both at EU level and at national level; deliver a strong mandate – echo what Tomas has said – on Europol; increase and ease the access to information, the exchange of that information for our security agencies, both at EU and national level; and improve the coordination between all relevant services that are there to protect children – law enforcement, the judiciary, the social services and health and education, and, of course, really beefing up the implementation of the DSA, also in relation to child exploitation here.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Madam President, organised crime has moved into the digital world, into the very space where our children learn, play and build their lives. We cannot accept a digital 'Wild West', where criminal networks are free to hunt for our children online.

In Sweden, since 2022, wherever Charlie Weimers from the Sweden Democrats now is – under your party and your party's friends, the far-right and the right government, we have witnessed a deeply disturbing reality: criminal gangs recruiting increasingly younger children to commit acts of violence through social media. Violence is commissioned with a click. And children are not only being recruited, they are being turned into recruiters. This is what political failure looks like when society does not protect children – organised crime steps in.

It is therefore important that the EU act now – we need a strong EU action plan and preventive actions, digital literacy, age verification on social media platforms, strong cross-border cooperation, more support to law enforcement and zero tolerance for tech companies profiting while children are recruited. Every day we wait, another child is at risk.

Car nous ne pouvons pas laisser le crime organisé voler l’avenir de nos enfants.

C’est vrai, le problème est complexe et il y a énormément de choses à faire. On l'a dit, mais je vois une mesure facilement atteignable à notre niveau, une occasion en or: la révision du mandat d’Europol, en y créant des unités spécialisées capables de détecter et de traquer les recruteurs en ligne. Car nous ne pouvons pas laisser le crime organisé voler l’avenir de nos enfants.

paragraphs.text: Chère collègue, je vous ai entendue sur les plateformes numériques. À Marseille, un gamin de 14 ans a exécuté un chauffeur de taxi, Nessim, âgé de 36 ans, en octobre 2024. Il a été condamné à 17 ans de réclusion criminelle.

Donc je suis assez étonné des discours «béni-oui-oui» qu'on entend ici. Je pense que dans cet hémicycle, je suis le seul à avoir été policier durant 20 ans dans les quartiers difficiles de France. Arrêtez les discours évangéliques ou angéliques et prenez la mesure du danger qui guette.

Est-ce que pour vous, un mineur qui tue, qui assassine, a sa place en liberté ou en prison? Soit en prison pour protéger les victimes, selon moi; soit être dehors pour refaire des victimes, selon vous. Parce que, à 13 ans comme à 17 ans, il faut que l'on protège nos citoyens de ces fous furieux armés qui, même très jeunes, peuvent exécuter.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, il fenomeno del reclutamento dei minori da parte della criminalità organizzata, certamente non nuovo, perché utilizzato dalle mafie, ha assunto oggi dimensioni e modalità allarmanti.

Come segnalato di recente da Europol, in tutta l'Unione le organizzazioni criminali reclutano sistematicamente bambini e ragazzi, coinvolti in più del 70 % dei settori criminali, per la commissione di reati sempre più violenti, come estorsioni e omicidi.

Le tecniche di reclutamento si fanno più sofisticate e subdole, con il massiccio ricorso ad app, social media e piattaforme online. I criminali, poi, manipolano facilmente i più giovani, adottando il loro stesso linguaggio e tecniche di cosiddetta "gamification".

Dobbiamo agire. Dobbiamo agire al più presto per prevenire e contrastare il reclutamento online e offline, perché un minore reclutato per commettere un reato è egli stesso vittima, la prima vittima di quel reato, in quanto sfruttato e privato della sua innocenza.

Bene, quindi, il piano annunciato dalla Commissione per la protezione dei minori dalla criminalità. Ma non basta: anche la futura direttiva contro la criminalità organizzata dovrà tenere conto di tale fenomeno, ad esempio con aggravanti specifiche per chi recluta minori.

Occorre però anche intervenire a monte su esclusione sociale, abbandono scolastico e prevenzione del disagio per creare prospettive di sviluppo e di crescita, perché l'illegalità trova terreno fertile dove i ragazzi non vedono vie d'uscita al degrado sociale e culturale.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario McGrath, existe un estremecedor reclutamiento significativo —y está creciendo— de menores de edad para la perpetración de delitos graves, tráfico de drogas y crímenes violentos. Incide en todos los Estados miembros, pero se ensaña particularmente con la Europa del norte, con algunos países escandinavos —Dinamarca, Suecia...—, y, por tanto, estamos obligados a actuar. Y este es el sentido de este debate: ¿qué hacer?

En primer lugar, el reclutamiento es en línea a partir de los trece años, y, por tanto, se debe exigir a las plataformas digitales sujeción estricta a la legalidad europea, al Reglamento de Servicios Digitales, que les obliga a eliminar los contenidos ilegales —y, desde luego, los que invitan al delito lo son—.

En segundo lugar, es necesario utilizar todos los datos que pone a nuestra disposición la Red Europea de Prevención de la Delincuencia para tomar conocimiento de cuál es la dinámica en la que incide este ensañamiento con los menores de edad, incitados a cometer delitos graves.

Pero, en tercer lugar, y por supuesto, debe haber prevención, lucha contra la exclusión, contra la marginación y contra la desigualdad, así como programas sociales de inclusión dirigidos a la protección de la infancia, como propone exactamente la Estrategia Europea para la Seguridad Interior: protección de los menores contra la delincuencia.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Europe is facing a terrifying new reality: organised criminal gangs are no longer recruiting only adults, they are recruiting children. Teenagers are being transformed into drug couriers, hitmen and instruments of terror in our own cities. In Sweden, for example, we have seen horrifying cases where boys as young as 13 or 14 were recruited by migrant gang networks to carry out shootings and bomb attacks linked to drug wars.

Children are exploited because criminal bosses know that minors often receive lighter sentences, and their suburbs have become breeding grounds for parallel criminal structures. In France, a second example, criminal organisations connected to narcotics trafficking have similarly used minors for violence, intimidation and street‑level drug distribution, particularly in areas overwhelmed by failed integration and uncontrolled migration.

We must finally speak honestly: this crisis did not emerge in a vacuum. Mass migration, failed integration policies and the creation of isolated communities have enabled organised crime to flourish across Europe.
Europe cannot...
